title.narrative: Strengthening Protection for Women, Girls, and Vulnerable Populations impacted by the conflict in Sudan through Integrated GBV, Shelter, and MPCA interventions in River Nile state

description.narrative: ltpgtAs reported by the IOM DTM Flash Report, it is estimated that between 20 October and 28 November 2024, a total of 393,337 individuals, representing 78,963 households, were displaced from various regions within Aj Jazirah state due to escalating hostilities between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). It has been reported that approximately 21 percent of individuals were displaced to the River Nile State, predominantly to the localities of Shendi, which accommodates 34,395 internally displaced persons (IDPs), and Al Matama, which hosts 19,060 IDPs. Substantial concerns pertaining to the protection of individuals have been articulated, as reports indicate the separation of IDPs from their family members, incidents of looting, and occurrences of sexual and gender-based violence (GBV). The principal needs of the majority of IDPs in River Nile State include access to food, suitable housing, safe potable water, sanitation facilities, in addition to health and protection services. Throughout this multi-sectoral project, the IRC's goal is to reach 8,390 IDPs, with theltspangt aim to improve the protective environment for adolescent girls in River Nile State and strengthen the capacity of community structures in the prevention and response to GBV through a community-based approach, to link women and girls to specialized services.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtFurthermore, the IRC will work with its local partner JASMAR Human Security Organization to enhance its ability to deliver timely and dignified CP services to affected population. ltspangtThe IRC and JASMAR, will provide contextualized lt/spangtltspangtand lt/spangtltspangtstructured psychosocial support (PSS) interventions to women and girls at the temporary Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS). Moreover, the IRC's Girl Shine curriculum, which aims to empower, protect, and support adolescent girls in humanitarian contexts, will provide interventions that are specifically designed for adolescent girls. These interventions will cover reproductive health (RH) and life skills. lt/spangtltspangtThe IRC will provide its partner with training on case management, GBV fundamental concepts, guiding principles, and safe referral mechanisms as a capacity-building measure. The IRC will also provide training to frontline GBV actors and community structures on the fundamental concepts and minimum standards of GBV. As part of the GBV risk mitigation initiative, the IRC and the partner will distribute dignity packages to the most vulnerable women and girls, including those with special needs (PSN), and conduct quarterly safety audits. Through focus group discussions, community members will be involved in the assessment of imminent risk, as well as in the observation and heightened awareness of GBV-related topics.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will meet the urgent shelter needs of conflict-affected IDPs in River Nile aligning with Shelter Cluster objectives. It will distribute 700 non-food items (NFIs), and provide Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to 250 households to restore basic living conditions. Distribution will prioritize safety, ensuring women and girls can access services without fear of violence. The shelter kits and hygiene items will enhance safety, dignity. and privacy reducing exposure to GBV. The IRC will implement a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning plan, incorporating field visits, regular reporting, and post-distribution monitoring. Additionally, a Complaint and Feedback Mechanism will be established to report misconduct. The project is expected to improve safety, well-being, and resilience among vulnerable women and girls, and simultaneously address the immediate repercussions of the conflict.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIn May 2025, after the liberation of Al Jazirah state by SAF, and following an assessment with authorities along technical consultations with SHF and relevant GBV AoR on change of targeted locations, it was endorsed by the GBV AoR to remain within the same Abu Hamed and Shendi localities, while expanding the targeted group to include IDPs from all-over Sudan.ltbrgtlt/pgt
